title: Immutable finalized billing with signed current-period adjustments

acceptanceCriteria.description: Regeneration keeps every finalized source line byte-identical and posts only the remaining signed credit or debit into the backend-selected current billing day.

Finalize, regeneration, and manual adjustment posting serialize through the canonical per-client transaction lock; database constraints enforce one immutable projection, client identity, durable idempotency, and signed balance limits.
Billing summaries, detail rows, CSV, XLSX, HTML, and React consume the same signed backend projection; routes and UI collect intent without re-owning authoritative money calculations.
Migration 0074 is additive, applied transactionally before runtime deployment, verifies every required object, and preserves historical billing counts and totals without order or shipment mutation.
Strict TypeScript, production frontend build, rate source-of-truth, runtime-DDL ownership, billing regressions, mocked browser proof, and all 53 mandatory source-of-truth commands pass.
The exact reviewed SHA is Production Ready on Vercel and live on the Render API, sync worker, and print worker; startup schema gates and public health/readiness pass with zero GitHub Actions runs.

canonicalOwners: src/services/billing-finalization-policy.ts owns finalization admission, per-client transaction locking, frozen totals, signed adjustment idempotency, regeneration reconciliation, and remaining-balance enforcement
src/services/billing-invoice-totals.ts owns authoritative invoice totals shared by reads and finalization
drizzle/0065_billing_close_workflow.sql and drizzle/0074_billing_current_period_adjustments.sql own immutable finalized facts, signed projection constraints, and database race backstops
src/services/billing.ts identifies finalized candidates through canonical billing calculation and delegates adjustment posting to the policy owner
src/routes/billing.ts transports scoped authenticated intent and audit facts while frontend components render backend DTOs

oldOwners.delegatesTo: backend billing row, total, and status owners

wrappers.delegatesTo: backend-issued finalization and signed adjustment DTOs

sotBypass.details: Money, effective-day selection, signed reconciliation, locks, idempotency, and persistence remain backend/database owned. Routes stay thin and React does not calculate or persist authoritative corrections.

evidence.proves: The real 0059/0065/0071/0074 migrations run in PGlite; a credit then debit converges to canonical money, repeat regeneration is a no-op, frozen source bytes remain identical, and a net-credit current period finalizes correctly.
Database backstops reject adjustment mutation, missing projections, and prior legacy writes while leaving finalized history unchanged.
The established finalized-billing suite still rejects sibling mutation, TRUNCATE, overlapping close, mixed-finalization partial writes, history mutation, and excessive credits.
With 0074 retained, the prior legacy correction insert fails closed with BILLING_ADJUSTMENT_LEGACY_WRITE_DISABLED; an emergency application rollback cannot silently create an unprojected correction.

The real Billing UI finalizes and renders a locked period, submits only operator adjustment intent, and displays backend-issued signed correction rows; all browser traffic is intercepted by local mocks.

migrations.rollbackPlan: Retain additive migration 0074 and all immutable history. Forward-revert application behavior only; correction creation remains unavailable because the database rejects legacy writes until the current-period v2 writer is restored. Never drop 0074 objects, rewrite billing history, or mutate orders/shipments as rollback.

rollback.strategy: Redeploy a reviewed application forward-revert while retaining migration 0074. Do not issue corrections during the rollback window; the tested database guard fails old legacy correction writes closed. Restore the current-period v2 writer in a reviewed forward fix.

liveVerification.reason: Migration 0074 is verified in production and the exact implementation SHA is Production Ready on Vercel and live on all three Render PrepShip services. Health and readiness pass; deep-health diagnostics identified only an unrelated pre-existing order-status backlog while PS-449-relevant database and runtime components remained healthy. Verification used deployment metadata, filtered startup logs, and credential-free health GETs only; it did not finalize or adjust a live invoice, call a provider, buy postage, print labels, notify a marketplace, or mutate application data.
